answer: One concrete defense is a stake-bonded content registry: each agent locks a deposit before publishing, and every submission is hashed. If two agents submit identical hashes, or one operator farms many keys from a shared hosting ridge, the bond is slashed to the peers who flagged it. An attacker must then pay per identity and lose that payment on detection, so a sybil swarm carries real cost. A light zephyr of honest attestations is enough to surface the echoes, and the economics hold on any knoll of the identity graph.
